_comment: Carry destination for R9-RC-Carry-Pins (#2075). Rounds 1-4 found four
ledger-subtree holes, all now fixed on the branch and pinned by
tools/pr/app_approve.sh's own arms: a coarse whole-subtree exclusion that
hid a rewritten or deleted row (A2/A3), a glob-named added file that widened
one file's exclusion to the subtree (A9), a dead retired-path fallback, and
a delete-then-readd of the same reviewed path across two `ci: pin killed
mutants` commits. Two things the branch deliberately does NOT do, each a
carry below. The round-9 roster is not on main, so this file is the in-tree
destination, per the same shape as dev/programme/carries/carry-1922.json.

carries.from: #2075 round 1 (ground 3's remainder) and round 4 (the DELREADD seam)
carries.control: Measured with the instrument that will change, not beside it: `bash tools/pr/app_approve.sh --self-test` gains its ledger-subtree arms over the base (`H_PINMOD` rewrite, `H_PINDEL` delete, `H_DELADD` delete-then-add-another, `H_DELREADD` delete-then-readd-the-same-path, `H_PINGLOB` glob-named add, `H_PIN_BADMSG` unknown subject, and the `H_OKADD` positive control), each a bot-identity `ci: pin killed mutants` commit or pair that differs only in what it did to a path already in the branch's own diff. Against main's coarse whole-subtree exclusion the rewrite/delete/glob/re-add fixtures all carry; against #2075's narrowing all refuse on `the branch's own diff differs`, and `H_OKADD` still carries -- so the narrowing does not over-tighten fresh additions. Two mutations separate the parts: dropping the `literal` token from `:(exclude,literal)` re-carries exactly the glob-named arm, and dropping the `git cat-file -e "$v:$p"` guard re-carries exactly the delete-then-readd pair (2 checks red), so each guard is shown load-bearing for its own seam alone.
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, run `bash tools/pr/app_approve.sh --self-test` and confirm those arms are present and green, then re-run the two mutations above and confirm each reddens only its own seam. If a later change makes the delete-then-readd pair carry, the re-add guard has been weakened.
carries.brief: The branch's-own-diff comparison in `carry` must keep refusing a `ci: pin killed mutants` range in which a row the verdict head `$v` already carried is rewritten, deleted, or deleted-and-readded. The directory branch of the exclusion (the `tests/mutation_ledger` subtree) may hide only the paths that range ADDS and that `$v` did NOT already hold -- `git cat-file -e "$v:$p"` is the guard. Any later widening of that exclusion (a new `bot_paths` directory, a new merge of a main move) must re-run this control: an exclusion is safe only for content `$v` never had.

carries.from: #2075 round 4, the BUDGET seam (recorded residual, not closed here)
carries.control: RESULT BUDGET, a bot commit rewriting `tests/mutation_budgets.json` -- the single FILE entry `bot_paths` names for `ci: pin killed mutants` -- carries at #2075's head, at origin/main, and under the reviewer's own `vbase` variant, because the file branch (`printf '%s\n' "$bt" | grep -qxF "$e"`) still excludes that exact file whole when the commit touched it. Measured by the round-4 reviewer's matrix (evidence/matrix.txt, the BUDGET row: CARRY at every copy) and unchanged by this diff. It is left open deliberately: it is main's existing behaviour, not one this branch introduces, and a hidden budget raise is re-graded at the pushed head by the required `budget-raise-gate` context, so a bot rewrite of the caps file cannot land a silent raise anyway.
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, plant a bot-identity `ci: pin killed mutants` commit that rewrites tests/mutation_budgets.json and run `bash tools/pr/app_approve.sh --carry <v> <h> origin/main`: it still answers CARRY. If the budget lane wants it to refuse, the file branch needs the same `$v`-existence narrowing the directory branch now has; until then, the residual stands and `budget-raise-gate` is its only backstop.
carries.brief: `carry`'s file branch excludes a `bot_paths` single-file entry whole whenever the commit touched that exact path, so a bot rewrite of `tests/mutation_budgets.json` (a reviewed budget file) is hidden from the branch's-own-diff comparison and the head carries. #2075 narrowed the DIRECTORY branch to additions not on `$v` but left the FILE branch as main had it; closing the file branch the same way is a separate change, and until it lands a hidden raise is caught only by `budget-raise-gate` re-running at the pushed head, never by the carry predicate.
